title: Jacaranda Health's PROMPTS, with an NLP-triaged helpdesk, improved knowledge and care-seeking in a 40-facility Kenyan cluster RCT (2021 to 2022)
summary: Kenyan cluster RCT (Nov 2021–Aug 2022): PROMPTS with NLP-triaged helpdesk raised knowledge and care-seeking indices by 0.06–0.09 SD
account: PROMPTS is an SMS platform for pregnant and postpartum women in Kenya run by Jacaranda Health. It combines informational messages, appointment reminders and a two-way clinical helpdesk. In the helpdesk, natural language processing (NLP) assigns each message an intent and priority level. Roughly 86% then get automated guidance; the rest are escalated to clinical agents. In an unmasked cluster randomized trial across 40 health facilities in eight counties, 6,139 pregnant women enrolled between 8 November and 10 December 2021. Follow-up ran to 24 August 2022. Treatment-facility participants had higher knowledge (0.08 SD), birth preparedness (0.08 SD) and routine care-seeking (0.07 SD) indices. Also higher: newborn care (0.09 SD) and postpartum care content (0.06 SD). Danger-sign care-seeking did not differ significantly. Effects are for the whole platform, not the AI component alone.
purpose: Deliver pregnancy and postpartum information by SMS and triage incoming questions to a clinical helpdesk by intent and priority.
system: PROMPTS: AI-enabled SMS platform with a natural language processing pipeline for helpdesk intent and priority classification
deployer: Jacaranda Health with Kenyan county health facilities
location: Eight counties (Kajiado, Kilifi, Kirinyaga, Kisii, Meru, Narok, Nyeri, Siaya), Kenya
taxonomy_note: The measured gains are maternal-health knowledge and care-seeking indices for the whole platform, not clinical outcomes.

ratings.reason: Effects are small average index shifts (0.06–0.09 SD) across a trial cohort, with no individual outcome attributed to the AI.
Aggregate trial result; danger-sign care-seeking showed no significant effect.

ai_role.statement: NLP triage decided the priority of helpdesk messages. The trial randomized the whole platform, so the AI's separate contribution to the measured effects is not identified. The trial was led by Harvard researchers (the first author and the two joint senior authors). Innovations for Poverty Action researchers (data curation, investigation, supervision) and five Jacaranda Health employees were among the co-authors. The USAID DIV and Gates Foundation grants were awarded to Rajasekharan and the Jacaranda Health team.

Impact evaluation of a digital health platform empowering Kenyan women across the pregnancy-postpartum care continuum: A cluster randomized controlled trial. PLoS Medicine 22(2): e1004527.

headline: PROMPTS raises knowledge and care-seeking in Kenyan cluster RCT
metric: raised knowledge and care-seeking indices by 0.06–0.09 SD

comparator.against: women enrolled at the 20 control facilities, where PROMPTS was not systematically introduced
comparator.before: control-facility participants (reference group; levels not reported in the abstract)
comparator.after: 0.08 SD higher knowledge index, 0.08 SD higher birth preparedness index, 0.07 SD higher routine care seeking index, 0.09 SD higher newborn care index, 0.06 SD higher postpartum care content index
comparator.quote: Participants recruited from treatment facilities had a 0.08 standard deviation (SD) (95% CI [0.03, 0.12]; p = 0.002) higher knowledge index, a 0.08 SD (95% CI [0.02, 0.13]; p = 0.018) higher birth preparedness index, a 0.07 SD (95% CI [0.03, 0.11]; p = 0.003) higher routine care seeking index, a 0.09 SD (95% CI [0.07, 0.12]; p < 0.001) higher newborn care index, and a 0.06 SD (95% CI [0.01, 0.12]; p = 0.043) higher postpartum care content index than those recruited from control facilities. No significant effect on the danger sign care seeking index was found (95% CI [−0.01, 0.08]; p = 0.096).

later.note: By the third quarter of 2025 Jacaranda Health reported 3,580,095 mothers reached cumulatively through PROMPTS across 23 Kenyan counties and 1,500 facilities, with over 200,000 added in the quarter and Ghana signing up for national scale-up; the trial paper itself had already noted over 2 million users added after November 2021.
later.quote: In Q3 alone, we reached over 200,000 additional mothers, the highest of any quarter to-date (p2), and received the green light in Ghana to scale nationally (p5).

revisions.change: Record drafted from the cited sources.

Reworded the helpdesk description so that roughly 86% of messages receive automated guidance and only escalations reach clinical agents, and restated authorship so that Harvard holds the first and joint senior authorships, the IPA authors did data curation, investigation and supervision, five authors are Jacaranda Health employees, and the USAID DIV and Gates grants were awarded to the Jacaranda Health team.
Benefit type set to Improved Physical Health under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Learning among the six first used.
Added what the benefit is measured against, what happened since from the cited sources.
Country of the developer and the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.
